correctness.rationale: Coupling Bin(3k,p) and independent Bin(3,p), cancelling internal tail terms, gives q_k-q_(k+1)=P(X=k)(1-p)R_k(p). The exact degree-two rational R_k has derivative (3k+1)(6kp-5k+4p-4)/(2(k+1)(2k+1)) <0 on (0,1/3] and R_k(1/3)=2(3k+2)/(9(k+1)(2k+1))>0. Within sizes 3j-2,3j-1,3j the threshold j is fixed and the upper-tail probability strictly increases; therefore every size is dominated by 3. Boundary p=0 is deliberately excluded. Independent rational recurrence checks 57 adjacent pairs; symbolic proof carries the continuum.
residual_risks: Finite rational checks cannot certify continuum of p; derivative proof does.

value.rationale: Closes a specifically posed subcritical continuum of the generalized Chaundy–Bullard binomial-tail problem, with strict order for every k and a unique equal-stake optimum, exceeding classical single-p endpoint. The restricted scope is mathematically meaningful even though general unequal-stake optimization is still open.

final_claim: For all k>=1 and real 0<p<=1/3, q_k(p)=P(Bin(3k,p)>=k) strictly decreases, so among equal-stake binomial averages at threshold one-third, unique optimum is m=3 and value 1-(1-p)^3. Does not optimize unequal stakes.
limitations: Only equal stakes at threshold 1/3, not arbitrary stake vectors.
No claim for p=0 where strictness fails.
